title: Effective fpqc descent for quasi-affine scheme morphisms
statement: Let $p:A\to B$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] whose one-member family is an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Let $V\to A$ be a quasi-affine morphism [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism]: the inverse image of each affine open in $A$ is a quasi-affine scheme, meaning a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme. Let $\phi:V\times_B A\xrightarrow{\sim}A\times_B V$ be an isomorphism over $A\times_B A$ satisfying $\phi_{02}=\phi_{12}\circ\phi_{01}$ on $A\times_B A\times_B A$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pd-descent-datum]. Then this datum is effective: there exist a scheme $V_0\to B$ and an isomorphism $V_0\times_B A\simeq V$ over $A$ inducing $\phi$. No local finite-presentation hypothesis on $V\to A$ is imposed. All schemes are in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention].

source.place: Tag 0247, lemma-quasi-affine, one-member fpqc covering specialization; used in Tag 02W8 for each saturated quasi-compact open.

proof.text: Use the property $\mathcal P(f)$ that $f$ is quasi-affine in the stated sense. It is invariant under isomorphism directly from the definition, and is stable under arbitrary base change by [lem-trf-quasi-affine-base-change]. This verifies condition (1) of the reduction lemma used in the last step.

source.place: Tag 0247, first paragraph of proof; Tag 02W3, condition (1)

proof.text: For a finite family $f_i:Y_i\to T_i$ with $\mathcal P$, let $T=\coprod_iT_i$. The component images are clopen by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. If $H\subset T$ is affine open, $H_i=H\cap T_i$ is clopen in the affine scheme $H$, hence equals a principal open $D(e_i)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent], and is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion]. Thus $f_i^{-1}(H_i)$ is a quasi-compact open in some affine scheme $Z_i$, by quasi-affineness. Their finite disjoint union is a quasi-compact open in the affine scheme $\coprod_i Z_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](4); it is precisely the inverse image of $H$. For no components the source and target are empty, and the same assertion holds with $\operatorname{Spec}(0)$. This proves condition (2) of the reduction lemma.

source.place: Tag 02W3, condition (2), verified for quasi-affine morphisms; Tag 0247, first paragraph

proof.text: We prove condition (3) for an arbitrary flat surjective morphism $p:A=\operatorname{Spec}S\to B=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and the given quasi-affine $V\to A$. Affine schemes are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so $p$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). This singleton is an fpqc covering: for every affine open $H\subset B$, its inverse image is quasi-compact, so finitely many affine opens of it cover it, and their images cover $H$ by surjectivity, as required by [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Since $A$ itself is affine, $V$ is a quasi-affine scheme. Put $C=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$. By [lem-trf-quasi-affine-canonical-affine-embedding], $V$ is qcqs and $j:V\to W$ is an open immersion. The ring map $S\to C$ defines $W\to A$, and $j$ is over $A$ because both composites $V\to A$ correspond to that same ring map by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]. The morphism $W\to A$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine].

source.place: Tag 0247, affine reduction and construction of W; properties.tex Tag 01P9 identifies this W over the affine A

proof.text: Write $A_2=A\times_B A$, with projections $p_i$, and $V_i=V\times_{A,p_i}A_2$, $W_i=W\times_{A,p_i}A_2$, for $i=0,1$. These projections are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], and $A_2$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-global-sections-qcqs] with $X=V$, $S=A$, $S\prime=A_2$: its qcqs hypothesis is Step 3. If $S_2=\Gamma(A_2,\mathcal O)$, it gives isomorphisms $C\otimes_{S,p_i^\sharp}S_2\simeq\Gamma(V_i,\mathcal O)$ with formula $c\otimes t\mapsto c|_{V_i}\,t|_{V_i}$. The affine fibre-product formula therefore identifies $W_i$ canonically with $\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(V_i,\mathcal O)$. Under this identification the base change $j_i:V_i\to W_i$ is the canonical map: both maps to the affine $W_i$ send $c\otimes t$ to $c|_{V_i}\,t|_{V_i}$, so equality follows from [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme].

source.place: Tag 0247, flat-base-change display and construction of the algebra isomorphism

proof.text: The datum $\phi:V_0\simeq V_1$ over $A_2$ induces an $S_2$-algebra isomorphism $\phi^\sharp:\Gamma(V_1,\mathcal O)\simeq\Gamma(V_0,\mathcal O)$. Apply the contravariant affine-spectrum functor [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and conjugate by Step 4 to obtain $\psi:W_0\simeq W_1$ over $A_2$. It extends $\phi$: $\psi j_0=j_1\phi$, since these maps into the affine $W_1$ induce the same ring map $\phi^\sharp$ on global sections, by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme].

source.place: Tag 0247, the isomorphism of algebras induces a datum on W and V to W is a morphism of data

proof.text: Check the cocycle on $A_3=A\times_B A\times_B A$. The maps $A_3\to A_2$ and $A_3\to A$ are flat by successive applications of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] (each forgets one or two factors of the flat map $p$), and their sources are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. The pullbacks of $V$ are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], applied over the affine qcqs schemes using Step 3. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-global-sections-qcqs] applies both from $A$ and from $A_2$. Its identifications commute with the ring maps induced by $\phi$: on each tensor generator $a\otimes t$ both orders send it to the pullback of $\phi^\sharp(a)$ times the pulled-back scalar $t$. The successive-base-change identifications also agree, since both send $(c\otimes s)\otimes t$ to the product of the three pulled-back sections. Consequently the pullback of $\psi$ along each $A_3\to A_2$ is the affine spectrum of the ring map induced by that pullback of $\phi$. Contravariant functoriality [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and the cocycle $\phi_{02}=\phi_{12}\phi_{01}$ give $\psi_{02}=\psi_{12}\psi_{01}$. Hence $(W,\psi)$ is a descent datum and $j$ is a morphism of descent data [def-pd-descent-datum].

source.place: Tag 0247, sentence asserting the induced algebra cocycle; tensor formula writes out its naturality

proof.text: Apply [lem-galois-fpqc-affine-descent-effective] to the affine morphism $W\to A$ and datum $\psi$, using the fpqc singleton checked in Step 3. Obtain $W\simeq W\prime\times_B A$ compatibly with descent data, for a scheme $W\prime\to B$. Let $q:W\to W\prime$ be the projection. It is flat and surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]; it is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), since $p$ is quasi-compact. No affineness assertion about $W\prime$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0247, apply lemma-affine and identify W with the base change of U-prime

proof.text: Let $O=j(V)\subset W$. Under the identification $W=W\prime\times_B A$, the two maps $r_0,r_1:W\times_{W\prime}W\to W$ correspond to the two pullbacks over $A_2$, with their identification given by $\psi$; this is the compatibility in Step 7 and the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Since $\psi j_0=j_1\phi$ and $\phi$ is an isomorphism, $r_0^{-1}O=r_1^{-1}O$. Here the images of $j_i$ are the inverse images of $O$: pullbacks of open immersions are open immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], and the universal property identifies them with the inverse-image open subschemes [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tag 0247, stability of the open V under the canonical descent datum

proof.text: The equality in Step 8 implies that $O$ is a union of fibres of $q$. Indeed, if $q(x)=q(y)=z$, the spectrum of $\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(z)}\kappa(y)$ is nonempty: it is the base change of the surjection $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)$ to the one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$, so [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] apply. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points] a point of this spectrum gives $t\in W\times_{W\prime}W$ with $r_0(t)=x,r_1(t)=y$. Step 8 then gives $x\in O\iff y\in O$. Set $U=q(O)\subset W\prime$; hence $q^{-1}U=O$. Since $q$ is flat, quasi-compact and surjective (Step 7), [lem-weil-pbc-flat-qc-surjective-quotient-map] shows that $U$ is open.

source.place: Tag 0247, invariant open is the inverse image of a subset U, and the fpqc projection is a quotient map

proof.text: Give $U$ its open-subscheme structure in $W\prime$ and its composite map to $B$. Its base change to $A$ is the open subscheme $q^{-1}U=O$ of $W$, by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] and the fibre-product universal property. The open immersion $j$ identifies $V$ with this open subscheme by [def-weil-open-immersion], giving $U\times_B A\simeq V$. On $A_2$ its canonical descent identification is the restriction of $\psi$, which by Step 5 is precisely $\phi$. Thus the isomorphism induces the specified datum [def-pd-descent-datum]. This proves condition (3). Finally apply [lem-galois-fpqc-descending-types-morphisms], with conditions (1), (2), (3) supplied by Steps 1, 2, 3–10. Its conclusion gives $V_0\to B$ and the required compatible isomorphism for the original, arbitrary singleton fpqc cover. None of the steps assumed local finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 0247, final identification of V with X times U; Tag 02W3 completes the affine reduction

proof_origin.place: Tag 0247, lemma-quasi-affine, entire proof, using Tag 02W3 for the reduction. Over the affine base its relative spectrum and sheaf flat-base-change argument are written with ordinary spectra and flat base change of global sections; the tensor formula explicitly verifies the cocycle.
